scenes.heading: Tables
scenes.narration: Tables are the objects you query in Databricks, and understanding their types helps you manage data and its lifecycle correctly.

scenes.heading: Types you will use
bullets: Managed tables owned by the metastore
External tables backed by your own path
Views that save a query definition
scenes.narration: Managed tables let the metastore own both the metadata and the storage location. External tables keep the data at a path you control while the catalog tracks the metadata. Views store a query definition rather than data, presenting a shaped result on top of underlying tables.

scenes.heading: Creating tables and a view
scenes.narration: The first statement creates a managed Delta table whose files Databricks controls. The second declares an external table pointing at an existing archive location. The final view saves a filtered query so users can select big orders without repeating the logic.

scenes.heading: Drop behavior differs
scenes.narration: Dropping a managed table removes both its metadata and its underlying data files. Dropping an external table only removes the metadata, leaving the files untouched at their location. Knowing this difference prevents accidental data loss and orphaned files.

scenes.text: Default to managed Delta tables; reach for external tables only when the data must live outside Databricks' control.
scenes.narration: Default to managed Delta tables for simplicity, and reach for external tables only when the data must live outside of Databricks control.
